title: My 12 Song Submission
excerpt:
Recently I had the most amazing opportunity to submit my application for a music coordinator role working for the amazing, multi-award winning music supervisor, Julia Michels! The opportunity came at a time I was also setting up this site and I couldn't think of a more perfect first piece to post then the 12 songs I submitted as part of interview process. It was hard to pick 12 songs. I didn't know what to land on because all of my favorite songs (800+) are just as special to me as the next one. There have been many iterations of this playlist too. But without further ado, here are my chosen 12!

 Happy listening 🤘🏼🎶
body:
1. Frank Zappa — [Watermelon in Easter Hay](https://open.spotify.com/track/0Q2dRzhPWFOex89dOjbq5Y?si=97bb65de1bb74f34)

This was one of the easiest decisions for this playlist and one of the most special songs to me. Watermelon in Easter Hay feels like a thank you and goodnight to music itself. Contextually, it's the moment in the album where Joe is about to give up on his music career and this guitar solo is his last. You can feel that in every note. There's something about it that makes me feel like I'm floating, like I'm witnessing someone giving absolutely everything they have left. It's devastating and beautiful at the same time, and I don't think I'll ever get tired of it.

2. Joyce Manor — [Catalina Fight Song](https://open.spotify.com/track/2TqfK2N1kFoX7OySPCB7pQ?si=162a3e48697e4605)

I knew making this list that a Joyce Manor song had to be on it. I grew up in a neighboring city to the band, and Catalina Fight Song opens with the lyric "sunken city by the ocean" — a landmark that was literally five minutes from where I grew up, in a small city called San Pedro. There is something about hearing a place you know immortalized in a song that never gets old. This one is short but mighty, and no matter how many times I've listened to it, it gets me riled up every single time. It's a piece of home, and as someone who grew up in the punk scene, I'm glad I get to put it on this list.

3. Abdel Halim Hafez — [Ahwak](https://open.spotify.com/track/1chsFxuRdocgGwhhCYfZ9m?si=7331791b5be8494b)

I wanted to include Ahwak because it is not just culturally significant to me, but because the composition makes me swoon every time. What this song does is take me back to a place I have never actually lived in — it is nostalgic for somewhere I only exist in through culture and memory. And although this is a love song, arguably one of the best ever written, I experience it as a song of pure appreciation. I owe that entirely to the composition. The lyrics are absolutely beautiful, and in a time where yearning feels increasingly rare, Ahwak reminds me that yearning is an art.

4. The Beach Boys — [Long Promised Road](https://open.spotify.com/track/4x3wjsXr6MtWNXii5gA1Ai?si=496e315420a14378)

Choosing between this and God Only Knows was genuinely difficult, but Long Promised Road holds a special place for me because it was one of the first Beach Boys songs I ever heard and loved. It is not the happiest of songs, though it can come across that way at times, and that duality is exactly what draws me to it. There is something deeply human about it. It captures the feeling of adulthood being completely overwhelming in a way that few songs do. I found myself returning to it during a difficult period in my life, and what surprised me was that I pulled something almost hopeful out of it rather than something heavy. It knocked me down and helped me back up at the same time.

5. Hayley Williams — [Love Me Different](https://open.spotify.com/track/5SxcXth9dGPlZ6khs3zcD9?si=a582dcb1c1864cc7)

It was hard to pick just one Hayley Williams song, but Love Me Different earned its place. There is something about it that makes me feel deeply feminine in the most grounding way — not performatively, just fully. The song captures something I live every day: the whirlwind of allowing people in and out of your life, of others assuming they know what is best for you, and the quiet resolve of realizing that you are the only one who actually does. What makes it rare is that it takes something painful and finds the relief in it rather than the wound. There is a moment where she sighs and it literally feels like exhaling — like the answer was never about being loved differently by someone else, it was always about showing up for yourself. I am glad a song like this exists.

6. The Stone Roses —[ I Wanna Be Adored](https://open.spotify.com/track/758wEKVqfYopJIHYWdLVd4?si=d96a50403e0c4300)

This song hits every time I'm in a room where I feel like a background character in my own story. It's a quiet reminder that my worth doesn't depend on whether someone else has caught up to it yet. The line "I don't need to sell my soul, he's already in me" has become a personal mantra for every moment I've been tempted to shrink or compromise just to earn approval. It's knowing yourself so clearly that you refuse to trade that away. Emotive, alluring, and psychedelic without doing too much, the lyrics are simple but the song is anything but. It's not a call to be loved, it's something more primal and unapologetic. There is something almost sinful about belting the outro, but in the way everyone sins. It is permission to want things without justifying yourself.

7. LCD Soundsystem — [All My Friends](https://open.spotify.com/track/2Ud3deeqLAG988pfW0Kwcl?si=ac8d1bd8a487419e)

All My Friends makes me want to be young and spontaneous, and then it breaks my heart a little. It is friendship and platonic love wrapped in something bouncy and alive, but this song finds me every time I catch myself wondering how I got here — when did everyone scatter, when did the nights that felt endless actually end, and why does it feel like I blinked and a whole chapter of my life just closed without warning. It's not sad exactly, it's more like standing in a doorway looking back at a room you loved and knowing you can't go back in. The building momentum mirrors exactly how time actually feels — slow forever and then suddenly fast, and then gone. It's the only song that's ever made me feel like the quiet grief of just drifting from people you loved is something worth naming.

8. Praise — [All in a Dream](https://open.spotify.com/track/59rJ1pQ2Rh4azHf1nxIX7j?si=5fdd2e70228d41eb)

Punk but so optimistic. This song makes me feel like I need to physically run the happiness off — it is liberating and hopeful in a way that is almost overwhelming. Every time it ends I want to go out and build something, connect with people, be part of a community, which has meant everything to me especially right now. In a time where the state of the world makes optimism feel naive, this song reminds me that it is actually a choice. The lyric "and through the darkness I'll choose to see the light" is not toxic positivity, it is a declaration. And I need that reminder more than I'd like to admit.

9. Devin the Dude — [What a Job](https://open.spotify.com/track/1QpMNpzkMxchOeYOn9RbNJ?si=5adc8a0262bd46d6)

There is something about this song that just gets it. The behind the scenes work, the thankless hours, the kind of commitment that most people on the outside cannot fully see or understand. What a Job captures what it actually feels like to be someone who loves music enough to build a life around it — not glamorously, just honestly. It is not a complaint and it is not a brag. It is just the truth, and that simplicity is what makes it stick.

10. The Rolling Stones — [Wild Horses](https://open.spotify.com/track/4M4Q3JLsUbyTkd5WHty1WB?si=ac0899b4eeea4fb9)

There is something deeply honest about a song that admits devotion and exhaustion can live in the same breath. I know this is not a deep cut and that it is deeply beloved by many, but I couldn't leave it off. Not many songs can make me cry the way this one does. When it comes on, my chest gets heavy and I can feel my heart trying to push through it. It is one of those songs that just holds so much, and somehow that is enough

11. Ella Fitzgerald —[ It Don't Mean a Thing](https://open.spotify.com/track/3LEAXQg3vnyLK184wPOGyT?si=d8ba2fa74e70451e)

I hunted this song down as a kid after hearing it in a show and not being able to rest until I found it. That experience is one of my earliest memories of music having real power over me. This song started something.

12. Little Simz — [Woman (ft. Cleo Sol)](https://open.spotify.com/track/60GM1mA58L7SYD1bLQXBho?si=0deed78bc21f43b7)

There is nothing quite like being in a room full of women who are genuinely rooting for each other — no competition, no scarcity mindset, just pure wanting to see each other win. I have been lucky enough to have that, and I have also been in spaces where it was noticeably absent, and the difference is everything. This song reminds me to be the person who makes other women feel seen, celebrated, and like there is enough room for all of us.\
\
\
I﻿ hope my 12 were just as exciting for you to listen to as it was for me to land on. I'm thankful for the opportunity to have my choices be reviewed by someone I look up to. So anyways...I gotta go on and get to my interview so toodaloo!
